item.title: Suva ready for Tailevu challenge in Skipper Cup Round 9
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026 Suva has named a formidable 23-member team that will take on Tailevu this afternoon in Round 9 of the Skipper Cup Competition.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026

Suva has named a formidable 23-member team that will take on Tailevu this afternoon in Round 9 of the Skipper Cup Competition.

Co-captain Isireli Fa will start at prop alongside Joseva Nasaroa, while Patemo Nuku is at hooker.

Nadidi Taginaselala will partner Kolinio Tamanitoakula at lock, while Viliame Tuwai and Daniele Natavo are the flankers.

Co-captain Mosese Naiova will start at number eight.

Joji Vusoniyasi will team up with Sakiusa Siqila in the halves, while Bronson Lee and Petero Misaele are on the wings.

Sanaila Daliga will combine with Rusiate Baletamavua in the centres, while Inia Tawale will start at fullback.

The reserves are Mikaele Delana, Mataiasi Tuisireli, John Filipo, Lesi Korovavala, Timoci Momolevu, Sevanaia Seviua, Savenaca Damudamu and Onisimo Dawalu.

Suva will face Tailevu at 3pm today at Nakelo School Grounds.

In other matches, Lautoka will meet Taveuni at Wairiki School Grounds, Nadi will meet Malolo at King Charles Park, Ba will take on Rewa at 4R Electric Govind Park, Naitasiri will face Nadroga at Ratu Cakobau Park, and Navosa will meet Kadavu at Lawaqa Park.

item.title: Fijiana XV set for Netherlands clash with key changes
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026 The Vodafone Fijiana XV have made a few positional changes to their starting line-up that will take on the Netherlands in the WXV Global Series Challenger this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026

The Vodafone Fijiana XV have made a few positional changes to their starting line-up that will take on the Netherlands in the WXV Global Series Challenger this afternoon.

Zipporah Sorokacika, who was on the bench last week, has been given the green light to start at loosehead prop, with Keleni Marawa at hooker.

Mereoni Nakesa comes into the side at lock, while Kolora Lomani starts at halfback, with Evivi Senikarivi providing cover from the bench.

Josivini Neihamu returns at inside centre, while Ivamere Nabura starts at fullback.

The reserves are Selai Naliva, Karalaini Naisewa, Adi Kelera Lawavou, Karavaki Lutumaibau, Nunia Daunimoala, Litiana Vueti and Vasemaca Dura.

The Fijiana will take on the Netherlands at 4pm today.

item.title: Nawaqanitawase double sends Roosters into NRL Grand Final
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026 Mark Nawaqanitawase scored a double to help the Roosters defeat the Dolphins 36-20 and reach the NRL Grand Final for the first time in eight years.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 26/09/2026

Mark Nawaqanitawase scored a double to help the Roosters defeat the Dolphins 36-20 and reach the NRL Grand Final for the first time in eight years.

The last time the Roosters made the Grand Final and won was in 2019, when they defeated the Canberra Raiders 14-8.

Sam Walker made a triumphant return from injury, scoring a try and converting two tries.

Other tries for the Roosters came from Victor Radley, Daniel Tupou, Robert Toia and Lindsay Collins.

The Roosters had too many weapons across the park, with Toia breaking eight tackles, Naufahu Whyte racking up 205 run metres, and Salesi Foketi and Reece Robson combining for 80 tackles.

In front of a sold-out crowd of 52,286, the Dolphins fought the game out to the end after making the finals for the first time in just their fourth season.

Jamayne Isaako scored a double, while Kulikefu Finefeuiaki and Herbie Farnworth scored a try each.

Meanwhile, the Panthers will face the Newcastle Knights at 6pm today.
